sentences: As a historian who's always searching for the text or the image that makes us re-evaluate the past, I've become preoccupied with looking for photographs that show our Victorian ancestors smiling (what better way to shatter the image of 19th-century prudery?).
I've found quite a few, and—since I started posting them on Twitter—they have been causing quite a stir.
People have been surprised to see evidence that Victorians had fun and could, and did, laugh.
They are noting that the Victorians suddenly seem to become more human as the hundred-or-so years that separate us fade away through our common experience of laughter.
translations: 作为一名总在寻找能让我们重新评价过去的文本或图像的历史学家，我一直专注于寻找展示维多利亚时代祖先微笑的照片（还有什么更好的方式能打破19世纪假正经的形象呢？）。
我已经找到了不少这样的照片，而且——自从我开始在推特上发布它们以来——它们引起了不小的轰动。
人们惊讶地看到证据表明维多利亚时代的人有乐趣，能够并且确实会笑。
他们注意到，随着分隔我们的百来年时光通过我们共同的笑声体验而消逝，维多利亚时代的人似乎突然变得更有人情味了。

sentences: Of course, I need to concede that my collection of 'Smiling Victorians' makes up only a tiny percentage of the vast catalogue of photographic portraiture created between 1840 and 1900, the majority of which show sitters posing miserably and stiffly in front of painted backdrops, or staring absently into the middle distance.
How do we explain this trend?
translations: 当然，我需要承认，我收集的“微笑的维多利亚人”只占1840年至1900年间创作的庞大摄影肖像目录中的极小一部分，其中大多数照片中的坐者要么在彩绘背景前痛苦而僵硬地摆姿势，要么心不在焉地凝视着中景。
我们如何解释这种趋势？

sentences: During the 1840s and 1850s, in the early days of photography, exposure times were notoriously long: the daguerreotype photographic method (producing an image on a silvered copper plate) could take several minutes to complete, resulting in blurred images as sitters shifted position or adjusted their limbs.
The thought of holding a fixed grin as the camera performed its magical duties was too much to contemplate, and so a non-committal blank stare became the norm.
translations: 在19世纪40年代和50年代，摄影术早期，曝光时间出了名地长：银版摄影法（在镀银铜板上生成图像）可能需要几分钟才能完成，导致坐者移动位置或调整肢体时图像模糊。
在相机执行其神奇职责时保持固定咧嘴笑的想法实在难以想象，因此一种不置可否的茫然凝视成了常态。

sentences: But exposure times were much quicker by the 1880s, and the introduction of the Box Brownie and other portable cameras meant that, though slow by today's digital standards, the exposure was almost instantaneous.
Spontaneous smiles were relatively easy to capture by the 1890s, so we must look elsewhere for an explanation of why Victorians still hesitated to smile.
translations: 但到了19世纪80年代，曝光时间快得多，而且盒式布朗尼相机和其他便携式相机的推出意味着，尽管以今天的数码标准来看很慢，但曝光几乎是瞬间完成的。
到19世纪90年代，捕捉自然的微笑相对容易了，因此我们必须从别处寻找维多利亚时代的人为何仍不愿微笑的解释。

sentences: One explanation might be the loss of dignity displayed through a cheesy grin.
"Nature gave us lips to conceal our teeth," ran one popular Victorian maxim, alluding to the fact that before the birth of proper dentistry, mouths were often in a shocking state of hygiene.
A flashing set of healthy and clean, regular 'pearly whites' was a rare sight in Victorian society, the preserve of the super-rich (and even then, dental hygiene was not guaranteed).
translations: 一种解释可能是，露齿的傻笑会显得有失尊严。
“大自然给我们嘴唇是为了遮住牙齿，”一条流行的维多利亚时代格言如是说，暗指在正规牙科诞生之前，口腔卫生状况常常令人震惊。
在维多利亚时代的社会，露出一口健康、干净、整齐的“珍珠白”牙齿是罕见的景象，是超级富豪的专属（即便如此，牙齿卫生也并非有保障）。

sentences: A toothy grin (especially when there were gaps or blackened gnashers) lacked class: drunks, tramps, and music hall performers might gurn and grin with a smile as wide as Lewis Carroll's gum-exposing Cheshire Cat, but it was not a becoming look for properly bred persons.
Even Mark Twain, a man who enjoyed a hearty laugh, said that when it came to photographic portraits there could be "nothing more damning than a silly, foolish smile fixed forever".
translations: 露齿的笑容（尤其是有牙缝或牙齿发黑时）缺乏品位：醉汉、流浪汉和音乐厅表演者可能会扮鬼脸，咧嘴笑得像刘易斯·卡罗尔笔下露牙龈的柴郡猫一样宽，但这对于教养良好的人来说可不是得体的样子。
即使是喜欢开怀大笑的马克·吐温也说，谈到摄影肖像时，“没有什么比一个永远定格的愚蠢、傻气的微笑更糟糕的了”。

sentences:
31. According to Paragraph 1, the author's posts on Twitter ____
A. changed people's impression of the Victorians.
B. highlighted social media's role in Victorian studies.
C. re-evaluated the Victorian's notion of public image.
D. illustrated the development of Victorian photography.
translations:
31. 根据第一段，作者在推特上的帖子____
A. 改变了人们对维多利亚时代人的印象。
B. 强调了社交媒体在维多利亚时代研究中的作用。
C. 重新评价了维多利亚时代人对公众形象的看法。
D. 说明了维多利亚时代摄影的发展。

sentences:
32. What does the author say about the Victorian portraits he has collected?
A. They are in popular use among historians.
B. They are rare among photographs of that age.
C. They mirror 19th-century social conventions.
D. They show effects of different exposure times.
translations:
32. 关于他收集的维多利亚时代肖像，作者说了什么？
A. 它们在历史学家中很常用。
B. 在那个时代的照片中它们很罕见。
C. 它们反映了19世纪的社会习俗。
D. 它们展示了不同曝光时间的效果。

sentences:
33. What might have kept the Victorians from smiling for pictures in the 1890s?
A. Their inherent social sensitiveness.
B. Their tension before the camera.
C. Their distrust of new inventions.
D. Their unhealthy dental condition.
translations:
33. 在19世纪90年代，什么可能使维多利亚时代的人拍照时不微笑？
A. 他们固有的社会敏感性。
B. 他们在镜头前的紧张。
C. 他们对新发明的不信任。
D. 他们不健康的牙齿状况。

sentences:
34. Mark Twain is quoted to show that the disapproval of smiles in pictures was____
A. a deep-root belief.
B. a misguided attitude.
C. a controversial view.
D. a thought-provoking idea.
translations:
34. 引用马克·吐温是为了表明，对照片中微笑的不赞成是____
A. 一种根深蒂固的信念。
B. 一种被误导的态度。
C. 一种有争议的观点。
D. 一种发人深省的想法。

sentences:
35. Which of the following questions does the text answer?
A. Why did most Victorians look stern in photographs?
B. Why did the Victorians start to view photographs?
C. What made photography develop in the Victorian period?
D. How did smiling in photographs become a post-Victorian norm?
translations:
35. 文章回答了以下哪个问题？
A. 为什么大多数维多利亚时代的人在照片中显得严肃？
B. 为什么维多利亚时代的人开始观看照片？
C. 是什么使摄影在维多利亚时期发展起来？
D. 照片中的微笑是如何成为后维多利亚时代规范的？
